name: The Stair Head's Pay
description: A month's pay for the Warden who keeps the top of the Hushline Stair, in a leather purse sewn shut and sealed with the Rest's wax. Sergeant Dole counted it twice in front of you and wrote the sum on the seal, which is his way of saying he trusts you and his way of making sure.

name: The Roll's New Page
description: A fresh page of the Roll of Names, copied at Wardens' Rest for the Stair Head's own book: every village in the Vale in Roll-Keeper Hesk's small hand, and at the foot, deeper than the rest, the four that have gone quiet. There is room under them. Nobody at the Rest said so.

name: Listening-Bell
description: A Sayers' listening-bell: a brass tuning bell the length of a finger on a handle of polished bone, the Circle's mark filed off the collar. Held to the ear it hums with whatever the stones nearby are saying under their breath, and under that, lower, with one held note that is louder when you point it south. Taken off a smuggler's boat under the Lamp.

name: The Unsaid Page
description: A page torn from a Tallymen's tithe-book: a village's debt, reckoned in the collector's neat hand to the last half-mark, and across it, in a different ink and a heavier hand, one word: UNSAY. Somebody has paid to have a village struck from the Charter's books. The village's name is at the head of the page. The courier who ran south at dawn carries the other copy.

name: The Collector's Key
description: A brass key on a greasy thong, warm from a sleeping Tallyman's waistcoat pocket: the key to the collector's stilt-house at Moreva, with the Charter's tally-mark stamped on the bow so that nobody could mistake whose door it opens. Sauve Mor says the lesson is not the key. The lesson is that he never woke.

name: The Collector's Tithe-Book
notes: The Rogue's first quest (first_rogue): in the collector's strongbox (core:loot/tithe_strongbox), taken in the_strongbox, handed to Sauve in report.
description: A Tallymen's tithe-book in oiled calfskin, the Delta round, every house on every landing and what it owes, in the collector's neat hand. Moreva's page says forty baskets more than Moreva caught. The Charter believes the book, not the eels. There is something folded into the back.
